differentiator: It runs a model bigger than any single machine can hold by splitting its layers live across a peer-to-peer mesh, served as one ordinary OpenAI endpoint.

concepts.name: The Oner (through the mesh)
concepts.world: You are a single token. The camera never cuts as it travels from your prompt, down through layers that live on different machines, and back out as one answer.
concepts.shows: The distribution is a JOURNEY, not a diagram. A continuous vertical camera glide through stacked beats -- your prompt in, peers holding the layers, the answer out -- so the viewer physically feels the model spanning machines.
concepts.money_shot: The oner flythrough: the centered line is bright and large while the peers recede in depth, and it lands on 'the answer returns'.
concepts.creator_repost: Neale's whole pitch is 'distributed AI for the people' -- a video that makes the mesh feel like one living machine flatters the idea, not the metrics.
concepts.stranger_stops: A camera moving through text you can read at a glance is rare in AI dev-tool clips; the motion itself is the hook.
concepts.argument: This is the only concept that dramatizes the ONE cool thing (a model living across machines) as something you travel through rather than look at. It kills the node-diagram cliche outright and uses a device the last dozen videos never touched.

concepts.name: One Box, No
concepts.world: A hard before/after. Your machine tries to hold the model and can't; the mesh holds it together.
concepts.shows: A split beat -- one machine 'not enough' beside the mesh 'enough' -- then the model runs.
concepts.money_shot: The split flip from red-fail to blue-live.
concepts.creator_repost: Clear and punchy, but it argues by contrast, not by showing the mechanism.
concepts.stranger_stops: The fail/succeed flip is legible in 2 seconds.
concepts.argument: Strong and simple, but it stays at the level of a claim (won't fit vs fits) and never lets you SEE the layers spanning peers. Keep the split as a supporting beat, not the spine.

concepts.name: The Handshake
concepts.world: A network operations feel -- peers discover each other over the mesh and light up 'connected'.
concepts.shows: Diegetic panes of peers joining, a green live-state flip, telemetry.
concepts.money_shot: Three peers flip to 'connected' and a big model's name resolves.
concepts.creator_repost: On-brand for a P2P project, but a dashboard reads as infrastructure, not wonder.
concepts.stranger_stops: Status lights flipping green is satisfying but familiar.
concepts.argument: Good texture for ONE beat (peers connecting), not enough as a whole. Fold it in as the diegetic scene before the oner.

wow_bets: The continuous-camera oner as the money shot -- a device nothing in the last 12 runs used, and it makes distribution felt, not diagrammed.
mesh-llm's native electric-blue-on-near-black with green 'connected' accents, over an aurora blue field that reads like a live mesh.
The split ('one box' vs 'the mesh') and a diegetic peers-connect beat feed INTO the oner, so the concept builds to the flythrough instead of front-loading it.
color_script: Two temperature beats across the runtime, steered off the last two videos (07-10 light teal, 07-11 dark warm orange): the body sits cool electric-blue on near-black; the peers-connect beat introduces a warm-adjacent green 'connected' pulse; the endpoint payoff flashes a BRIGHT full-bleed blue field (inverted, dark ink). Blue accent is >=60 off orange-17 and flips canvas value vs the 07-10 light run, so the color gate clears.

light_plan.s1_two_line: large bright cream hero lines on near-black; the friction stated in bright ink
light_plan.s2_split: two bright value cards, the 'mesh: enough' card lit in accent-ink blue
light_plan.s3_mono_block: bright cream mono lines, the mechanism; accent-ink on the key line
light_plan.s4_panes: diegetic peers; a green 'connected' state flip is the bright element
light_plan.s5_oner_money: the centered glide line is large and bright cream, a real light source at the frame center
light_plan.s6_flash: the inverted BRIGHT beat -- full-bleed blue field, dark ink; the frame's brightest moment
light_plan.s7_logo_reveal: bright cream wordmark on near-black, holds the after-state

brightness_note: Dark canvas, no shader (07-11 used it). Brightness earned by design: aurora blue field lifts the base, plus >=3 genuinely bright beats (s5 oner centered line, s6 full-bleed blue flash, s1/s3 large bright hero type). Targets >=30% bright scenes so the frame-brightness gate passes without lifting in the grade.
